content:
The image shows a corn plant with clear light green to yellow streaking along the leaf veins, running the length of the leaves. The streaks form a mosaic/mottle pattern with alternating green and pale/yellow areas. The plant looks somewhat stunted compared to the healthy plant in the background. No pustules, spots, smut galls, or ear/stalk rot are visible.

Key features:
- Light green to yellow streaks along leaf veins
- Mosaic/mottle pattern on leaves
- Possible mild stunting
- Whole plant affected (systemic)

This matches **Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus**: "Narrow, light green to yellow streaks along leaf veins... mosaic or mosaic patterns... chlorotic spots and streaks on young leaves progressing to mottle or mosaic pattern."

It also partially resembles Maize_Streak_Virus, but that class is not in the provided list. Stewart's Disease shows bleached streaks but also has vascular discoloration. The pattern here — fine vein-parallel streaking with a mosaic quality — fits MDMV best among the available classes.
